strengths: QuEST offers a useful practical contribution: selectively finetuning temporal and attention-related layers, together with activation scales, using model-generated calibration data. Updating fewer than 7% of LDM-4 parameters provides an economical approach to low-bit diffusion quantization.

The empirical gains are meaningful across multiple datasets and generation tasks. At W4A4, Table 3 reports FID improvements over EfficientDM from 10.60 to 5.64 on LSUN-Bedrooms and from 14.34 to 11.76 on LSUN-Churches. ImageNet sFID also improves from 9.28 to 7.93. The default evaluation uses 50,000 generated images.

The ablations support the usefulness of the components. In Table 6, adding temporal and critical-module alignment improves FID from 6.95 to 4.41 and then 3.26. Table 7 supports combining local and global supervision, while the activation analyses provide an intuitive motivation.

The manuscript is generally well organized, cites the principal datasets and competing methods, and provides a code link. Its discussion of possible effects on watermarking and safety checking identifies relevant societal considerations.
weaknesses: The efficiency evidence needs reconciliation. For W4A8 LDM-4, Table 6 reports 15.25 GPU-hours with FID 3.26, whereas Table 8 reports 0.45 hours with FID 3.82. The manuscript does not explain the different protocols or which initialization, calibration, and optimization stages are included. Because efficient finetuning is central to the contribution, this ambiguity materially limits assessment of its advantage. More complete stage schedules, batch sizes, and quantizer specifications would also improve reproducibility.

Theorem 3.2 is not established by the supplied derivation. Each Taylor step in Eq. (11) uses the quadratic term involving the incremental perturbation epsilon, whereas Eq. (10) substitutes an accumulated activation residual, which is generally different. No explicit remainder or Hessian bound supports the subsequent dismissal of the second-order term. Section 3.4 appropriately disclaims a guarantee, but the theorem and stronger theoretical claims still require correction. This concern does not itself invalidate the empirical results.

Originality lies primarily in the particular module selection and progressive alignment scheme: temporal sensitivity and efficient quantization-aware finetuning are already represented by the cited TFMQ-DM, TDQ, and EfficientDM work. The ablations demonstrate that adding components helps, but lack comparisons against alternative layer subsets with the same parameter budget or simultaneous alignment. Consequently, the specific selection and ordering are less firmly justified than the overall finetuning approach.

The Stable Diffusion evaluation is substantially weaker than the LDM evaluation: Table 5 reports only CLIP Score and compares only against Q-Diffusion. CLIP Score does not establish image fidelity or diversity. Moreover, remaining degradation is substantial in some W4A4 settings, including ImageNet IS falling from 364.73 to 202.45 and Stable Diffusion CLIP Score from 31.50 to 28.85. These results support improved low-bit generation, but claims of preserving full-precision performance should be qualified.
